tutorial.title: Parameterized Queries
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to build complex queries using SQLite in Express

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent: When writing SQL in Express, we can utilize parameterized queries to make database access as flexible as possible.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Parameterized queries are a type of SQL query in which placeholders are used for values, which are passed as parameters.

They are used to make working with data convenient but also to prevent SQL injection attacks.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
We have a connection to a database that has a users table with values inside.

We can now create an SQL query to retrieve an entry.

Make sure to pick SELECT *, followed by FROM users, and finally WHERE name = 'Alice'.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You have a database connection and a users table containing data.

Write a query that selects every column from users whose name is Alice.

Make sure to pick SELECT *, followed by FROM users, and finally WHERE name = 'Alice'.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Before we can run it, we need to prepare it with db.prepare.

Make sure to pick db, followed by ., and finally prepare.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Prepare the shown statement on db without running it yet.

Make sure to pick db, followed by ., and finally prepare.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
To keep a reference of our query, we save it in a variable.

Make sure to pick const, followed by query, and finally =.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Save the prepared query as query and prevent reassignment.

Make sure to pick const, followed by query, and finally =.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Finally, we can run it and log the result.

Make sure to pick query, followed by .get().
lessons.hardModeContent:
Retrieve one matching row as an object from query and log it.

Make sure to pick query, followed by .get().

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
However, a much better approach is to use a parameterized statement with a ? that we can later replace with the actual value.

Make sure to pick WHERE name = ?, followed by "Alice".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use a parameterized statement with ? so you can pass the actual value when you run it.

Use the parameter to retrieve Alice as a single row object.

Make sure to pick WHERE name = ?, followed by get, and finally "Alice".

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the main advantage of using parameterized queries?

They make queries reusable and prevent SQL injectionsThey allow the use of more complex queries

They make queries reusable and prevent SQL injections.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A user enters Alice" OR 1=1 as a name. The query uses WHERE name = ? and passes that input as the value. What is the advantage?

The input stays a value instead of changing the SQL, and the prepared query remains reusableThe input becomes part of the SQL condition so it can match every userThe placeholder automatically removes every quote from the stored name

The input stays a value instead of changing the SQL, and the prepared query remains reusable.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the query.

Make sure to pick WHERE followed by category and then =, ?.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the query.

Make sure to pick Database, followed by WHERE, category, =, and finally ?.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is a parameterized query?

A query where placeholders are used for values that are provided when the query is executedA query that automatically fetches parameters from the database

A query where placeholders are used for values that are provided when the query is executed.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which example prepares a parameterized query and supplies Alice when it runs?

prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?"), then get("Alice")prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = 'Alice'"), then get()prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = Alice"), then get(?)

prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?"), then get("Alice").

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the parameterized query.

Make sure to pick ?, followed by 123.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use a parameter to retrieve one order for customer 123 as an object.

Make sure to pick ?, followed by get, and finally 123.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
When using parameterized queries, we can also use multiple placeholders. However, we must keep the order in mind!

Make sure to pick ? followed by ? and then "Bob", 25.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can use multiple placeholders in a parameterized query. Keep their order in mind.

Retrieve Bob, aged 25, by binding the name first and age second.

Make sure to pick ?, followed by ?, "Bob", and finally 25.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's try using three parameters in the statement.

Make sure to pick ? followed by ? and then ?, "Laptop", 999.99.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Bind Laptop, price 999.99, and category Electronics to the three parameters.

Make sure to pick ?, followed by ?, ?, "Laptop", and finally 999.99.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also pass the parameters in an array to the get function, but we still need to keep the order in mind.

Make sure to pick ? followed by ? and then "1984",, "George Orwell".
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can pass the parameters in an array to get. Keep them in the same order as the placeholders.

Find the book titled 1984 by George Orwell. Bind title before author in the array.

Make sure to pick ?, followed by ?, "1984", and finally "George Orwell".

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
When creating endpoints, we often use the route or query parameters to identify the element that we want to get, update, or delete.

In this case, we use the id route parameter to create a query based on our client's needs.

Make sure to pick id, followed by id = ?, and finally req.params.id.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use route or query parameters to identify the entry you want to get, update, or delete.

Here, use the id route parameter to query the entry your client requests.

Make sure to pick id, followed by id = ?, and finally req.params.id.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
Sometimes, we may want to use more than one ? in a statement. Let's look at an example where we receive three values from the client.

Make sure to pick ? followed by ? and then ?, req.body.name, req.body.age, req.params.id.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can use more than one ? in a statement. Here, you receive three values from the client.

Bind name and age from the request body, then id from the route parameter.

Make sure to pick ?, followed by ?, ?, req.body.name, req.body.age, and finally req.params.id.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do you pass multiple values into a parameterized query?

You use multiple ? placeholders and provide an array or argumentsYou concatenate the values into the SQL string

You use multiple ? placeholders and provide an array or arguments.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The query is UPDATE users SET name = ?, age = ? WHERE id = ?. Which call binds Mia, 24, and 7 correctly?

query.run("Mia", 24, 7)query.run(7, "Mia", 24)query.run(24, "Mia", 7)

Make sure to pick query.run("Mia", 24, 7).

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
Is it possible to pass an array of values to a parameterized query?

Yes, you can pass an array of values to a parameterized query, and each element will correspond to a ? placeholder in the queryNo, you need to pass each value individual as parameter

Yes, you can pass an array of values to a parameterized query, and each element will correspond to a ? placeholder in the query.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A query has placeholders for name, age, and id, in that order. You pass ["Mia", 24, 7]. How are they bound?

Mia to name, 24 to age, and 7 to idThe entire array is bound only to the name placeholderThe values are reordered by type before they are bound

Mia to name, 24 to age, and 7 to id.

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Set the name and the id to update the name of the user with a given id.

Make sure to pick ? followed by ? and then req.body.name, req.params.id.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Update the user identified by the route id with name from the request body.

Make sure to pick ?, followed by ?, req.body.name, and finally req.params.id.

lessons.interactiveContent:
Execute the query with the route parameter as argument.

Make sure to pick query, followed by ., and finally get.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Retrieve a single product as an object from the prepared query using the route parameter.

Make sure to pick query, followed by ., and finally get.
